about.text: The complainant is GlobalFoundries U.S. Inc., a Delaware corporation headquartered in Malta, New York, which describes itself as a leading American semiconductor manufacturer that grew out of AMD's manufacturing arm and IBM's microelectronics business, and which has invested heavily in U.S. manufacturing, including its Fab 8 facility, as a major recipient of CHIPS and Science Act funding. The respondents are eight companies in the Tower Semiconductor group: Tower Semiconductor Ltd. (Israel), Tower Partners Semiconductor Co., Ltd. (Japan), Tower Semiconductor Italy S.r.l., and five U.S.-based Tower entities (Tower US Holdings, Tower Semiconductor San Antonio, Tower Semiconductor NPB Holdings, Tower Semiconductor Newport Beach, and Newport Fab LLC). GlobalFoundries describes Tower as a smaller company with far less patenting and R&D investment than itself.

The investigation, instituted by the Commission, covers semiconductor devices and methods of manufacturing them that GlobalFoundries says use technology covered by six of its patents: the '235 patent (nickel silicide layers designed to prevent degradation when stress liners are removed), the '983 patent (high-voltage transistors with self-aligned channel wells for low resistance and high breakdown voltage), the '425 patent (self-aligned liners on metal-semiconductor contacts), the '546 and '167 patents (contacts formed in dielectric layers with intermix regions at the substrate interface), and the '748 patent (guard-ring and chip-edge seals using low-K dielectric to block moisture). The accused products are semiconductor wafers, chips, and components made using Tower's RF, power management, BCD, logic, SiGe, and BiCMOS processes, exemplified by three purchased products: a Qorvo evaluation kit, a Qorvo RF power tracker, and a Denso blind-spot-monitor sensor containing Tower-made dies.

allegations.text: GlobalFoundries alleges that Tower violates Section 337 by importing into the United States, selling for importation, and selling after importation semiconductor devices that infringe the specified claims of each of the six asserted patents. It identifies specific accused dies and products for each patent: devices made with Tower's RF processes, including the Qorvo QM81026 Power Tracker, allegedly infringe claims of the '235 patent; the PA22BZ die made with Tower's BCD process, found in the Qorvo evaluation kit, allegedly infringes claims of the '983 and '748 patents; and the M7DN25PS die, found in the Denso sensor and the Qorvo power tracker, allegedly infringes claims of the '425, '546, and '167 patents.

To show the accused products actually enter the United States, GlobalFoundries points to purchases of the Qorvo evaluation kit and RF power tracker in the United States (with import tariffs applied to the former, and the latter as a component of a smartphone assembled in India), and to a Toyota vehicle sensor containing the Denso part, photographed as made in Japan and purchased in Maryland.

GlobalFoundries contends it satisfies the domestic industry requirement -- the requirement that a complainant show its own significant U.S. activity tied to the patented technology -- through its manufacturing, design, and engineering operations across six U.S. facilities since 2012 and its substantial ongoing R&D investment in RF and power management process technologies.

GlobalFoundries asks the Commission for a limited exclusion order (an order barring specified infringing imports from a named respondent, as opposed to a general exclusion order covering all sources) blocking entry of infringing semiconductor devices made by or for Tower, cease and desist orders barring Tower from importing, selling, marketing, or otherwise commercially dealing in the accused products within the United States, and a bond on infringing imports during the 60-day period in which the President may review any remedy the Commission orders. GlobalFoundries has also filed a parallel patent infringement suit on the same patents in federal district court in the Western District of Texas.

paragraphs.text: The Tower respondents, all eight named entities, admit they manufacture semiconductor wafers in the United States, Italy, Japan, and Israel but deny that they themselves manufacture, import, or sell the three specific accused end products (the Qorvo evaluation kit, the Qorvo power tracker, and the Denso sensor), and deny importing those products into the United States at all. They deny infringing any claim of any of the six asserted patents, directly or indirectly, literally or under the doctrine of equivalents, and deny that GlobalFoundries has established the required domestic industry, disputing the substance of GlobalFoundries' claim charts. Tower asserts that all asserted claims are invalid under the patent statute's requirements for patentable subject matter, novelty, non-obviousness, written description/enablement, and correct inventorship, citing prior art (technology predating the patents) listed in an appendix, and raises further defenses of license or patent exhaustion, prosecution history estoppel, ensnarement of prior art under the doctrine of equivalents, and a challenge to GlobalFoundries' standing or ownership of the patents. Tower also argues that the relief GlobalFoundries seeks would not serve the public interest and should be denied, and it notes GlobalFoundries' parallel Texas federal lawsuit while denying that suit has merit; Tower reserves the right to add defenses as discovery proceeds.

answers.who: Tower Semiconductor Ltd., Tower Partners Semiconductor Co., Ltd., Tower Semiconductor Italy S.r.l., Tower US Holdings, Inc., Tower Semiconductor San Antonio, Inc., Tower Semiconductor NPB Holdings, Inc., Tower Semiconductor Newport Beach, Inc., and Newport Fab LLC

summary.headline: GlobalFoundries U.S. Inc. accuses eight Tower Semiconductor-affiliated companies of violating Section 337 by importing and selling semiconductor devices made with Tower's RF, power management, BCD, logic, SiGe, and BiCMOS manufacturing processes that allegedly infringe six GlobalFoundries patents on chip fabrication technology; the case is now pending before the ALJ.

standing.text: The investigation is pending before the ALJ, with discovery only recently begun. The Office of Unfair Import Investigations, the Commission's investigative staff, is not participating as a party, leaving GlobalFoundries and the eight Tower respondents as the only parties. No summary determination rulings, initial determination, or Commission decision have yet issued; all patents, claims, infringement, validity, and domestic industry issues remain to be decided.
